tasks.title: Ship 3 librarian agents + MCP servers: self-updating project indexes, selectable in /init-team, wired to the lanes that consult them
notes: USER: deferred by request ('later once you finish'). Queued behind T8.

REFERENCE PATTERN (read from '/home/ubuntu/source/Appnext Campaign AI/campaign-ai-platform/.claude/agents'): _librarian-template.md (canonical, 190 lines), history-librarian.md, tests-librarian.md, compliance-officer.md (55KB). Shape of each: haiku model; tools Glob/Grep/Read/Bash/Write/Edit; owns a private memory dir .claude/agent-memory/<name>/ holding an append-only commits.jsonl plus rolling summary_overall.md and summary_by_file.md; SELF-UPDATES incrementally on every invocation (e.g. git log since the last indexed hash); answers FROM memory via a bash search helper so the caller never pays for raw git output; explicitly does not touch production code, bump versions or push. Descriptions carry 2-3 <example> blocks so the orchestrator auto-delegates. Librarians consult each other (compliance-officer consults tests-librarian).
GOAL: teamme maps the project once via librarians instead of every generated agent re-deriving the same map its own way. The librarians are the project-comprehension layer, not roster filler.

OPEN DESIGN QUESTIONS for the future brief: (1) 'gate' needs defining - MCP tool-level refusal like teamme_install (precedent now exists in T8) vs a hook, which invariant #1 forbids from blocking; (2) 'self-updated autonomously with hooks' needs a trigger that cannot loop (invariant #2) and cannot block (invariant #1) - SessionStart is the safe candidate, PostToolUse is not; (3) which 3 - the reference set is git-history, tests-coverage and compliance, but teamme's own layer boundaries may imply different ones; (4) a librarian's memory is per-project state: committed or gitignored? (5) invariant #4 - librarian prompts are project-agnostic templates, their INDEXES are project-specific.

HISTORY-LIBRARIAN SCOPE (user, for the future brief): go beyond answering 'what changed in file X'. Two capabilities: (1) build a codebase MAP from historical changes read chronologically - the commit stream is the evidence, so structure emerges from how the code actually evolved rather than from a one-off static scan; (2) print a COMPLETE DEPENDENCY TREE of anything - workflow -> references -> scopes -> features -> tests, with the tests leg answered by consulting the tests-librarian rather than re-deriving it. That cross-librarian consultation is the pattern already present in the reference implementation (compliance-officer consults tests-librarian) and is what makes the map cheap: each librarian owns one axis and is asked, never re-computed.
Related: T27 (cross-project grants) may be the access-control layer this needs - librarian indexes are the obvious cross-project payload.

STORAGE DECISION (user's steer): back the librarian indexes with sqlite3, which is in the PYTHON STANDARD LIBRARY (3.45.1 on this machine) - so a real indexed DB costs no dependency and invariant #3 still holds. This is a material upgrade on the reference implementation's append-only jsonl + bash grep helper: it makes the indexes queryable rather than searchable. The dependency tree the user asked for (workflow -> references -> scopes -> features -> tests) is a recursive CTE, which SQLite does natively; jsonl cannot express it without rebuilding a graph in memory each time.

SCOPE CORRECTION: indexing needs NO cross-project identity. A librarian's DB lives inside the project (.claude/agent-memory/ or beside it) and is isolated positionally, exactly like worklog.json. The identity problem I raised applies only to T27 (sharing across projects), not to building the indexes.

WHAT TO INDEX (user): code, git history, bugs. Natural tables - commits (hash, author, date, scope tag), files_changed (commit -> path), symbols/imports/references (the dependency graph), tests (test -> source edges, coverage gaps), and the work log's own tasks, which already exist and could join to the files a task touched. The MCP server is the natural owner of the connection: it already runs as a process holding the project path, so it can expose query tools instead of every agent shelling out to grep.

HONEST GAP IN MY GROUNDING: I read _librarian-template.md and the headers of history-librarian.md and tests-librarian.md, but NOT compliance-officer.md (55KB) in full. The future brief must read it properly - it is the largest of the four and the one that shows how a librarian is consulted BY another agent rather than invoked directly.

FULL SPEC (user, verbatim intent): teamme provides OUT-OF-THE-BOX native indexing via a local DB owned by the MCP server. Capabilities: codebase mapping; a workflow expert; links between every aspect of the project; mapping existing tests to code, components and features; reported bugs too if an issue-tracking librarian is enabled; and a TREE MAP OF GIT HISTORY driven by reasoning about what actually happened in each commit - so any aspect of the development is easy to query, related changes are visible, and commit messages act as a STORYTELLING tool giving precise understanding of when, what and WHY a change was made. Self-refreshed on each plan before it is marked resolved, via hooks acting as gates that enforce committing the refreshed indexes along with the change.

STORAGE FORK (user): make it selectable whether the librarians' data is committed with the code or lives alongside it uncommitted. Applies to ALL generated knowledge - librarian indexes, the MCP server's knowledge base, and the agents' memories - not just one of them.

DESIGN TENSION 1 - a SQLite file cannot be committed sanely. It is binary, so git cannot merge it: two teammates indexing different commits produce divergent files that conflict irreconcilably, and every reindex churns the whole blob. This is probably WHY the reference implementation chose append-only commits.jsonl plus rolling markdown summaries - those merge. Likely resolution: keep the COMMITTED artifact append-only text (jsonl/markdown) and treat SQLite as a locally-rebuilt query layer derived from it. That satisfies both halves of the user's fork: committed-with-code means the text artifacts, uncommitted means gitignore them and rebuild locally. Do not commit the .db.

DESIGN TENSION 2 - 'hooks acting as gates that enforce committing' vs invariant #1: invariant #1 governs the WRITE GUARD (PreToolUse must fail open). A Stop hook that refuses to end a turn is a different, already-sanctioned mechanism - worklog-enforce.py stop already blocks on an active task. So an index-freshness gate belongs on Stop, not PreToolUse, and must obey invariant #2: state what re-arms it or it traps the session. The T10 lesson applies directly - stamp against a status-change field, never a mutation timestamp, or refreshing the index re-arms the nag that demanded the refresh.

REFRESH COST: 'self-refresh on each plan' must be incremental (from the last indexed commit, as the reference implementation does), never a full rescan - this runs inside the user's editing loop. Budget it like preflight: a hook that adds perceptible latency to every turn will be disabled by users, and a disabled gate enforces nothing.

*** TITLE IS NOW WRONG - READ THIS FIRST *** The task title says 'selectable in /init-team'. The user has corrected that: librarians are NOT team members and NOT offered in the roster questionnaire. Two tiers: (1) TEAM AGENTS - generated per project by /init-team, do the work; (2) LIBRARIANS - shipped BY THE PLUGIN, not generated, enabled/disabled per librarian at the PLUGIN level, with their own rules, skills and hooks. When enabled, team agents CONSULT them as a quick grounded source of truth. Out-of-the-box means exactly this: present without being chosen, not an extra roster lane.

REVERSES A RECORDED DECISION: CLAUDE.md 'Decisions already made' states 'The plugin ships no agents/ of its own by design - teams are generated per project'. Librarians would be the FIRST plugin-shipped agents. The user owns that call, but the brief must REPLACE that decision entry with the new reasoning (why librarians are shipped where teams are generated: they are project-agnostic machinery, not project-specific roles) rather than leave the docs contradicting the code. Also note the consequence the old decision flagged - nothing validates generated agent files - now partly changes, because shipped librarians CAN be validated by validate.sh like any other shipped file.

OPEN: librarians 'have their own hooks'. teamme today ships hooks only as TEMPLATES copied into a project (.claude/hooks/). A plugin-shipped agent's hooks could instead be plugin-level (a hooks/hooks.json in the plugin, which the harness loads directly) - a mechanism teamme has never used. Decide which, and note that plugin-level hooks are NOT copied per project, so enable/disable has to gate them at runtime rather than by presence.

A fourth librarian was specified after this task was written and lives in T30: a session librarian that indexes the chat history itself, continuously, so context lost to compaction can be fetched back by mark point. Same machinery as these three, different source class (the conversation, not the repo) and a different storage answer (never committable). Whatever schema and enable/disable mechanism T14 lands must accommodate it rather than be retrofitted for it.

GROUNDING GAP CLOSED - compliance-officer.md read properly (the note above admitted it had not been). Four findings that change the design: (1) DISCOVERY PRIMITIVE, NOT A LIST - the reference never hardcodes the librarian set, it globs .claude/agents/*-librarian.md, so a new librarian comes under enforcement with zero wiring. This is teamme's own T23 lesson arrived at independently: never derive a verdict from a list that grows. (2) CONSULTATION IS ENFORCED BY CITATION - a plan touching a librarian's scope must cite that librarian's answer ('COVERED by ...' / 'GAP: ...'); skipping it is a BLOCKED verdict. The enforcement is a review rule, not a hook. (3) STALENESS IS A MACHINE-READABLE MARKER - one HTML comment line '<!-- knowledge-freshness: indexed_hash=<sha> -->' near the top of each MEMORY.md, compared against git rev-parse HEAD. (4) The reference caps its rolling summaries (200 and 500 lines) so a consult has bounded context cost.

THE LOOP BUG, ALREADY SOLVED IN THE REFERENCE - and it is teamme invariant #2 in another costume. check-knowledge-freshness.sh counts commits since the marker with '-- . :!.claude/agent-memory' because a refresh's OWN commit touches only agent-memory; without that exclusion the refresh that clears the gate re-arms it and the gate can never reach FRESH. Identical in shape to stamping against status_changed rather than updated (T10). Whatever teamme builds must exclude the librarians' own store from its own staleness computation, and validate.sh must assert that a refresh actually clears the gate - the test that would have caught T10.

HARNESS CONSTRAINT, verified against the installed CLI (2.1.281) and decisive for 'librarians have their own hooks': a PLUGIN-shipped agent file has its 'permissionMode', 'hooks' and 'mcpServers' frontmatter IGNORED - the binary warns verbatim 'Plugin agent file ${e} sets ${Yt}, which is ignored for plugin agents. Use .claude/agents/ for this level of control.' So a librarian shipped in the plugin's agents/ CANNOT carry per-agent hooks. Per-librarian hooks therefore need either plugin-level hooks/hooks.json (which the CLI does load - the string appears 24 times, and there is a plugin-agents loader too) and which is global to the plugin rather than per-agent, or the existing template-copy route into .claude/hooks/. This makes the ship-vs-copy question below a real architectural fork, not a packaging preference. Also noted: agent frontmatter has a 'memory' field with a validated enum - worth reading before inventing a memory layout.

ARCHITECTURE DECIDED (user, this session). (1) WHERE: librarians ship in the plugin's own agents/ - the first plugin-shipped agents, reversing the CLAUDE.md 'ships no agents by design' entry, which must be REPLACED with reasoning (project-agnostic machinery, not project-specific roles). (2) NO LIBRARIAN HOOKS AT ALL - this dissolves the harness constraint instead of working around it. Librarians are QUERY-ONLY, each backed by its own store. (3) LIBRARIAN AGENTS ARE THE ONLY CALLERS of the librarian MCP tools; team agents consult librarians, never the DB. Team agents therefore need no new tool access and their tool lists stay tight. Existing teamme_worklog/teamme_intake_phase keep their current callers - this rule governs the NEW query tools. (4) GATING LIVES WITH THE TEAM AGENTS that consult librarians, in .claude/hooks/ where teamme's hooks already live. (5) GATE STRENGTH: 'ask' on git push (PreToolUse narrowed to git push), matching the reference implementation - so a hotfix proceeds with a conscious approval. Needs an explicit carve-out in CLAUDE.md invariant #1: 'ask' on a Bash command is not a write-deny, but the invariant's wording does not currently distinguish them.

CONSEQUENCE of query-only librarians, and it is a good one: the INDEXER IS A SCRIPT, NOT AN AGENT. Mechanical extraction (hash, date, author, subject, files, diffstat) is deterministic python3, costs no model call, and can be driven by a hook later without putting a model in the editing loop. The librarian AGENT supplies the reasoning layer the user asked for - scope tags, related-change grouping, and the commit-message-as-storytelling 'why' - when consulted or on an explicit refresh. Two-speed refresh, and only the cheap speed can ever run per-turn. The reference implementation has exactly this split: commits.jsonl carries mechanical fields plus reasoned scope_tags.

PHASE 1 SCOPE (approved): the substrate only - no agents, no gate, no new project-copied files. Deliberate: the indexer and store live in the PLUGIN (server/librarian/), invoked by the MCP server, so nothing joins REQUIRED_HOOKS. That avoids T23's trap by construction rather than by remembering - a copied indexer would make every future librarian grow the required-hooks list again. Deliverables: SQLite schema + rebuild-from-text, incremental git indexer, MCP query/refresh/status tools, validate.sh coverage including 'a refresh clears the staleness signal' (the assertion that would have caught T10), and a MEASUREMENT on this repo of cold index, warm refresh and query latency. Phases 2-5 (librarian tier, remaining librarians, gate, session librarian T30) are specified but not dispatched; the measurement decides whether they proceed as designed.
Phase 1 dispatched as T31 (librarian substrate). T14 stays open as the umbrella for phases 2-5.

PHASE 1 VERIFIED LIVE UNDER THE REAL HARNESS, which nothing had done before - validate.sh drives the tools over a test pipe, not through Claude Code's own MCP client. teamme_status: live, 6/6 hooks matching the plugin's copies (freshness resolved via the MCP server's own path hint, the first resolution rung). teamme_librarian_status on an unindexed project: correctly reports no data and names the refresh tool rather than erroring. teamme_librarian_refresh: full index of this repo in 0.117s, 12 commits / 136 file changes. teamme_librarian_query commits_touching on preflight.py: 5 rows with subjects and +/- line counts, which read as the actual development story of that file. The tool descriptions carry the INTENDED CALLER convention and say plainly that phase 1 does not enforce it.

CORRECTION to note ~22 and to how I have been describing it: plugin-shipped agents do NOT have permissionMode/hooks/mcpServers ignored *silently* - the CLI prints a warn-level message naming the ignored key. The constraint is unchanged (a plugin agent still cannot carry its own hooks, which is why librarians are query-only), but the hazard is narrower than I stated: it is visible at load time, just not caught by anything in this repo.

tasks.title: Cross-project shared knowledge: explicit per-project grants with read-only vs write, over the MCP server
notes: USER'S IDEA: teamme's MCP server could hold data across projects as shared knowledge, but only for projects the user explicitly grants, and with read-only vs write chosen per grant.

GROUNDING - the capability already exists, unscoped: teamme_mcp.py:133 takes project_dir from tool args (falling back to CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR then cwd) with NO validation, so teamme_worklog can already read and write any project's ledger on disk. Not a privilege escalation - the server runs as the user and the agent has Bash anyway - but undirected: nothing scopes it, nothing records consent, nothing reports afterwards that another project was touched. So the work is constraining and curating an existing capability, not adding one.

DESIGN QUESTIONS for the brief: (1) where do grants live? Per-project (.claude/) means a project declares who may read IT, which is the right direction for consent, but the server must then read the target's grant file, not the caller's. (2) Read-only vs write is only meaningful if the server enforces it - a prompt-level rule is not a permission. (3) What is actually shared? The work log is project-specific and low value cross-project; the interesting payload is closer to T14's librarian indexes. Consider whether T27 is the transport layer for T14 rather than a separate feature. (4) Revocation and staleness: a grant to a project that no longer exists, or was renamed. (5) An explicit deny-by-default, since today's behaviour is allow-everything.

tasks.title: Session librarian: index every session turn as it happens, so context lost to compaction can be fetched back by mark point instead of re-reading the transcript
notes: USER SPEC, verbatim intent: 'add auto-compaction session indexing as a librarian which can go back and fetch context from any session before compaction happened, and get it after compaction. by without requiring to read all the session, by indexing all the parts of a session (chat history) and store mark points in db. then there won't be any need to tell you to prepare for compaction, every step in a session will be indexed and added to the db of the plugin's mcp server.' The goal is explicit and testable: after a compaction, a question whose answer exists only in the pre-compaction region should resolve from the index, without re-reading the transcript.

GROUNDING, verified this session: session transcripts are real files on disk, one JSONL per session, under a per-project slug directory - this session is ~/.claude-personal/projects/-home-ubuntu-source-teamme/87e18ef7-....jsonl, and the conventional location ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/ also exists on this box with entries for other repos. JSONL is append-only, so indexing is incremental by byte offset: the indexer never re-reads what it already consumed. That is what makes 'index every step' affordable, and it is the same incremental property T14 needs for the code index.

VERIFIED, not assumed: the installed CLI (2.1.281) contains the hook event names PreCompact, SessionEnd, SubagentStop and PostToolUse alongside the four teamme already uses (grep -ao against /home/ubuntu/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.281: PreCompact 39 hits, SessionEnd 54, SubagentStop 56, PostToolUse 189). So a compaction boundary IS observable to a hook. Confirm the payload shape and the settings key against the docs before wiring it - presence of the string proves the event exists, not what it hands the script.

DESIGN, the load-bearing decision: indexing must be CONTINUOUS, and PreCompact must be only a boundary MARKER, never the indexer's trigger. Indexing at PreCompact would just relocate 'prepare for compaction' into a hook - same single point of failure, now invisible: one slow or failed run and the entire window is gone precisely when it can no longer be recovered. Continuous is also the only shape that matches the user's words, 'every step in a session will be indexed'. The tick can come from hooks teamme already owns (UserPromptSubmit, Stop) plus SessionEnd for a final flush; each run only consumes bytes appended since the last offset. PreCompact then writes one row saying 'everything before here is no longer in context', which is exactly the mark point retrieval needs to answer 'what did we lose'.

TENSION 1, storage: this is the one librarian whose index must NEVER be committable. T14 offers a choice - commit the librarians' knowledgebase alongside the code, or keep it beside the repo. For the session index that choice must not exist. A transcript contains everything anyone typed into the session, including secrets pasted in by accident, and indexing it creates a second copy that outlives the paste-cache. It lives machine-local, gitignored, with no cross-project grant under T27 unless the user asks for that specifically and separately. Also worth deciding: a retention bound, since an unbounded index of every session on the machine grows forever.

TENSION 2, the retrieval contract is the whole feature and the easiest part to get wrong: a fetch must return a BOUNDED slice. A tool that answers 'what did we decide about X before compaction' by handing back 40k tokens of transcript has reproduced the problem it exists to solve - it just moved the cost from re-reading the file to re-reading the reply. The index needs to store enough per mark point (turn boundary, tool call, file written, task status transition, compaction boundary) to answer WHERE something was discussed, so the fetch can be a targeted range and not a dump. Define what a mark point is before writing any schema - that definition IS the design.

RELATION to T14: same machinery (plugin-shipped, enabled/disabled at plugin level, not roster-selectable, SQLite from the stdlib, consulted by team agents), different source class. The other three librarians index the repo - versioned, shareable, reconstructible from git. This one indexes the conversation - unversioned, private, machine-local, and gone if not captured as it happens. That asymmetry is why it is a separate task rather than a fourth bullet on T14, and why its storage answer differs from theirs.

tasks.title: Librarian substrate (T14 phase 1): SQLite store rebuildable from append-only text, incremental git indexer, and MCP query tools - no agents, no gate, nothing copied into projects
notes: Parent: T14 (umbrella, stays open). Phases 2-5 remain specified-not-dispatched in T14's notes; T30 is the session librarian. READ T14's notes 20-25 before starting - they carry the reference-implementation findings, the harness constraint on plugin agents, and the architecture the user approved this session.

BUILT (phase 1 substrate, uncommitted): plugins/teamme/server/librarian/{__init__,store,history}.py plus three MCP tools (teamme_librarian_status/refresh/query) in teamme_mcp.py, and .gitignore entries for the derived index. Nothing copied into a target project, nothing added to REQUIRED_HOOKS - the indexer runs inside the MCP server, so T23's growing-list trap is avoided by construction.

MEASURED (in-process, so interpreter start is excluded). This repo, 10 commits/122 file rows: cold full index 0.137s, warm refresh 0.010s, rebuild-from-text 0.045s, queries 0.03-0.10ms. A 10,393-commit repo (local clone of vllm, 52,947 file rows): cold 15.0s ONCE, incremental +50 commits 0.40s (~8ms/commit), warm refresh with nothing new 0.012s, rebuild-from-text 1.26s, commits_touching 9-11ms, recent 0.09ms. Artifacts at that scale: commits.jsonl 9.0 MiB, index.db 22 MiB. VERDICT: phases 2-5 proceed as designed - a per-turn refresh costs ~12ms when idle, which is well inside preflight's budget.

CONTRADICTS T21's premise: python3 -c pass measured 23-42ms today on this machine (7 runs), not ~1.1s. sqlite3 import 43ms, importing the librarian package 56ms. Whatever T21 hit was not reproducible today - worth re-checking before any other decision leans on that figure.

PROVEN by hand, not yet by validate.sh: rebuild-from-text (db deleted, rebuilt, commits/files_changed/commit_parents rows and the marker byte-identical, at both scales); unreachable marker after a force-push falls back to full AND says so; empty repo = success with zero rows; not-a-git-repo and git-missing = clean error payload; malformed JSONL line skipped not fatal; CORRUPT index.db is discarded and rebuilt rather than raising; 10 concurrent refreshes leave no lock/tmp debris and no duplicate rows; a race while 5 commits land writes each commit exactly once; paths with newlines/quotes, non-UTF-8 bytes, binary files (NULL counts), merges (no file rows) and renames all parse. GAP FOR VALIDATION: scripts/validate.sh compiles plugins/*/server/*.py, which does NOT reach server/librarian/*.py.

VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY by the orchestrator, not taken on report: (1) validate.sh passes, exit 0. (2) py_compile clean on all three new files plus teamme_mcp.py. (3) The reported validate.sh gap is REAL - line 45's glob 'plugins/*/server/*.py' expands to teamme_mcp.py only and never reaches server/librarian/*.py. (4) REBUILD-FROM-TEXT re-run from scratch with PATH stripped to /nonexistent so git was genuinely unavailable: db deleted, rebuilt from commits.jsonl alone in 0.038s - 10/10 commits, 122/122 files_changed, 9/9 commit_parents, rows tuple-identical, marker preserved. (5) No truncation: git rev-list --count HEAD == 10 == rows in db, oldest and newest subjects match the real first and last commits. (6) Warm refresh 0.021s. MEASUREMENT VERDICT STANDS: an idle refresh is ~12-21ms and ~8ms/commit incremental even at 10k commits, so phases 2-5 proceed as designed. The only expensive operation is the one-time cold index (15s at 10k commits).

validate.sh: fixed the server/*.py glob (find -path, catches server/librarian/*.py - old glob only ever matched teamme_mcp.py, confirmed by direct expansion and by a scratch syntax-error fixture the old form missed and the new form caught). Added 9 librarian assertions to the throwaway-project smoke test: rebuild-from-text vs ground truth from git directly (not self-comparison) with PATH stripped; empty-repo/not-a-repo/missing-dir/git-missing as 4 distinct non-overlapping errors; unreachable-marker fallback naming rebase/force-push; corrupt index.db discarded-not-raised through teamme_librarian_query then rebuilt via an instructed refresh; 10 concurrent refreshes -> exactly 8 commits, no lock/tmp debris; commits_behind_head 2->0 after refresh over the pipe; hostile content (newline path, non-UTF-8 subject, merge commit = 2 parent rows/0 file rows); and a combined MCP-pipe block (all 3 tools respond, unknown query, bad hash, limit clamp+truncation, garbage line exits 0 empty stderr). Gaps still open: no assertion for phase 2's reasoned records being preserved through rewrite_records (no phase-2 code exists yet); commits_touching/search_subjects/commits_between query variants are exercised manually but not asserted; shallow-clone behavior untested.

VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY (validation lane): validate.sh passes, exit 0, 32 sections, 10.3s total (was ~5.2s, so the 9 new librarian sections cost ~5s of real fixture work - throwaway git repos and real MCP subprocess round-trips, not interpreter overhead). mtimes confirm the lane boundary held: validate.sh 18:50, server files 18:33-18:35, so the validation lane touched nothing but its own file. tasks.title: Librarian tier (T14 phase 2): ship the first plugin-shipped agent - a history librarian - plus the per-project enable/disable mechanism, the consultation contract team agents follow, and the storage fork
notes: SCOPE, and why it is one librarian and not three: phase 1 built ONE index (history). Shipping a tests-librarian or code-librarian agent now would be a prompt with nothing behind it - an agent that can only say 'I have no data'. Phase 2 therefore ships the HISTORY librarian only, and with it the whole tier mechanism (plugin-shipped agents/, per-project enable/disable, the consultation contract, the storage fork). Phase 3 then adds each further librarian as index+agent together, which the mechanism makes cheap. This also means phase 2 delivers the user's storytelling capability WITHOUT any new indexing: the agent reads commits from the existing index and reasons at query time. Stored reasoned enrichment (the 'kind' seam store.py already preserves through a full reindex) is an optimization, not a prerequisite - defer it.

MECHANISM DECIDED (orchestrator's call, routine): (1) CONFIG lives at .claude/librarians/config.json, per project, owned by the MCP server - which also sidesteps T32, since a Bash-less agent can reach it through a tool instead of editing a file. (2) DISABLED cannot mean absent: a plugin-shipped agent is visible in every project once the plugin is installed and cannot be hidden per-project. So disabled means the librarian tools REFUSE for that librarian, naming how to enable it, and the agent prompt checks status first - the same shape as the existing teamme_install gate, which is honest about being a refusal rather than a harness guarantee. (3) STORAGE FORK is a config key, not a doc instruction: commit_record true|false, defaulting to FALSE (do not commit). teamme writes or removes the .gitignore entry for commits.jsonl to match, so the choice is enacted rather than merely recorded. Default false because until the phase-4 freshness gate exists, a committed index only goes stale on every commit that does not refresh it - the reason this repo's own record was untracked in 5ea3e23.

PROMPT SIDE LANDED (note recorded by the orchestrator - the prompt lane has no Bash, which is T32 again): plugins/teamme/agents/history-librarian.md is teamme's first plugin-shipped agent - query-only, model sonnet (deliberately not the reference's haiku, because the mechanical extraction is already done by server/librarian/ and what is left for the agent IS the reasoning), no permissionMode/hooks/mcpServers per the verified plugin-agent constraint, memory omitted because the enum is computed in the CLI bundle and cannot be read by grep - and because the agent persists nothing anyway. Disabled is handled as a status-first refusal that RELAYS THE TOOL'S OWN WORDING rather than inventing an enable command, and explicitly forbids routing around a disabled librarian by reading git another way. Consultation contract added to init-team.md's shared guardrail block and templates/intake.md step 1, as instruction not gate, with the escape hatches written in. The prompt lane hand-traced the intake state machine to confirm its insert adds no branch that could leave a begin unmatched.

VALIDATION LANE landed and verified independently: 41 sections (was 34), ALL CHECKS PASSED, 10.5s. Watch-fail proofs on the disabled gate, commit_record enactment and the never-delete-a-foreign-line case - each broken, seen failing with the message quoted, reverted. I verified the reverts held rather than trusting them: no permissionMode in the shipped agent, no stray skills/stray.md, no .bak/.orig debris, and the whole suite green (the mutations were designed to BREAK things, so survivors would have failed it). Two things worth keeping: (1) the manifests check now WALKS the plugin tree with rglob and exits loudly on any *.md it does not know how to validate, so a third prompt directory cannot pass silently - the third time this repo has had to replace a narrow glob with a walk. (2) git check-ignore is the ground truth for commit_record, not the .gitignore text, so the assertion tests the effect rather than the intent. I corrected one string myself (validate.sh:128 said the CLI 'silently ignores' the forbidden keys; it warns) - my wording, my fix.
